transcript:
Header: 2026-12-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Ravi (BluePeak Head of AI), Emily (Infra), Noah (Product)

Summary (auto): scoping POC focused on cost modeling and unit economics. discussed baseline traffic, average tokens per request, batching and caching knobs, and POC benchmark plan + timeline. customer constraints: budget cap, on-prem vs hosted preference, security review. next steps and owners agreed.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll go over scoping for the POC focused on cost modeling and unit economics. quick intros?
00:08 Ravi: hi i'm ravi, i run the ai team at bluepeak, we do recommendation and search models across retail catalogs. emily and noah here as well.
00:15 Emily: hi all, infra lead, i'll own data/traces and sandbox setup.
00:20 Noah: product, i'll help define success criteria and user flows.
00:24 Jordan: jordan from redwood, i'll own the benchmark and infra side, hi.

02:12 Maya: cool, first high level - what's the workload shape? ravi?
02:18 Ravi: so production query profile is about 2k qps at peak across our global edge but for the POC we want to scope a 5 to 50 qps slice, realistic steady state for pilot is 15 qps. typical request is a prompt + user metadata, average tokens in is about 80 tokens, average gen out is 120 tokens, so ~200 tokens per request.
02:45 Jordan: ok 200 tokens per request at 15 qps is about 2.6M tokens per day (15 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 200 ~ 259,200,00 wait uh math, let me re-run) sorry, quick calc: 15 qps * 200 tokens = 3,000 tokens/sec -> 259.2M tokens/day, oh that's big, did i drop a zero?
03:05 Maya: yeah that sounds high. ravi is it 15 requests/sec or 15 requests/min?
03:10 Ravi: ah sorry, 15 rps is peak for the pilot cluster, for the initial POC slice let's do 5 rps sustained average, peak 15. so baseline target 5 rps steady, 5 * 200 tokens = 1,000 tokens/sec -> 86.4M tokens/day. still big. maybe we should do smaller, our initial trial wants to validate cost model at about 1M - 5M tokens/day for POC.
03:33 Emily: to be clear our budget for the pilot is approx $10k/month for inference incl. egress, so we need a per-token estimate that maps to that.
03:40 Maya: good, excellent - that'll drive hosted vs dedicated tradeoff.

05:05 Jordan: here's how we model unit economics for the POC: we look at three configurations - hosted (Redwood API), dedicated (reserved GPU pool), and private (VPC/on-prem evaluation). each has different fixed vs variable cost. for hosted we show per-token billing, for dedicated we amortize reserved GPU cost + infra + ops over tokens.
05:25 Jordan: rough numbers for discussion (ballpark): hosted generation tier = $0.50 per 1k tokens (so $0.0005 per token). with basic batching and caching enabled you can often lower effective cost by ~25-35% depending on hit rate. dedicated reserved GPU amortized could get us to about $0.20-$0.30 per 1k tokens ($0.0002-$0.0003/token) once you hit sustained volume and fully utilize the instance.
05:48 Ravi: can you show an example mapping to our $10k budget?
05:52 Jordan: sure. if we assume hosted list price $0.50/1k tokens, 1M tokens/day ~ 30M tokens/month -> 30M * $0.0005 = $15,000/month, that's above budget. but if we only do 5M tokens/month -> 5M * $0.0005 = $2,500/month. so pick volume matters. with batching and prefix/KV cache hits say 40% effective reduction -> the 30M case drops to $9k/month effective.
06:20 Maya: exactly, caching can make a big difference for repeated prefixes in search & rec. in practice, we see 20-50% savings depending on how much shared context you have.
06:30 Emily: what about latency SLA impacts when you batch aggressively? we can't degrade P95 too much. our SLOs are p50 <150ms and p95 <450ms for recommendations.
06:40 Jordan: good point - batching reduces per-token cost but can increase p95 if you wait to form batches. Redwood supports continuous batching with small windows (5-20 ms) and dynamic batching that keeps p95 within configured SLOs. for many configs we can keep p50/p95 within your targets, but we'll need to test with your distribution. quantized models and GPU kernel selection also matter.
07:05 Noah: any numbers on batching improvement?
07:08 Jordan: rough rule of thumb: batching 4-8 requests gives ~1.5-2.2x throughput efficiency depending on model and seq lengths. that translates to 30-55% cost reduction if batching opportunities exist.
07:20 Ravi: KV cache, how are you counting savings? we have a lot of repeated product-context prefixes in rec generation.
07:27 Jordan: KV (K V) cache - when the prefix tokens can be reused we only pay for the new tokens and the attention compute for cached keys is cheaper. typical effective token reduction is proportional to prefix length; if prefix is 60 tokens and new generation is 120 tokens, caching can reduce compute by ~33% for that request. aggregated across traffic with 40% cache hit rate that could be ~13% overall savings, again workload dependent.

09:12 Maya: so for POC we'll run 4 benchmark variants: 1) baseline hosted with no batching/cache, 2) hosted with batching tuned, 3) hosted with batching + KV cache warm, 4) dedicated reserved instance with production-like concurrency and quantized model. we'll measure cost, latency (p50/p95), throughput, and error rates.
09:35 Emily: for the dedicated case what infra cost assumptions?
09:40 Jordan: for the POC we can spin a dedicated 4-GPU cluster (A100x4 or equivalent) in Redwood Dedicated; reserved cost for a month we estimate ~$32k/month list for the hardware, but for POC we'll do a 2 week eval and amortize. the per-month number scales down in our modeling; important thing is utilization. if you fully utilize it for 24/7 inference, your per-token goes down to the $0.0002 range.
10:05 Ravi: that capex seems high but if utilization is right it makes sense. our POC timeline is 3-4 weeks to decision ideally.
10:12 Maya: proposed timeline: week 0 (this week) - kickoff and share artifacts, week 1 - infra setup + data ingest, week 2 - run 72h benchmark across variants, week 3 - analyze + review w/ stakeholders + security signoff, decision by end of week 3. is that aligned?
10:28 Noah: yes that works for product.
10:30 Emily: need to loop in security for VPC and KMS discussion, we may need SOC2 docs and SSO/SAML integration details.
10:36 Maya: we'll share our security pack and SOC2/ISO docs.

12:00 Jordan: benchmark plan details i'll send - items included: sample prompt set (we'll use 5k representative queries), traffic replay from prod traces (anonymized), token distribution histogram, and success criteria matrix. success criteria we propose: cost per 1k tokens <= $X given config, p95 latency under 450ms, quality judged by echo test score and product metrics (CTR uplift threshold or hit rate).
12:35 Ravi: on quality - we need to ensure no user-visible regressions. we'll provide a small human-eval prompt set (100 queries) to validate.
12:40 Maya: perfect. for cost target can you share what $X should be?
12:44 Ravi: given budget we want effective cost below $0.25 per 1k tokens for the POC if possible. that would map to ~ $7.5k/month for 30M tokens? (math discussion) we can confirm numbers.
13:00 Jordan: ok we'll map scenarios to that threshold. for example: if hosted list $0.50/1k -> need 50% effective reduction via batching/cache/quantization to reach $0.25/1k. dedicated may hit it at moderate utilization. we'll provide side-by-side calc table.

15:22 Emily: for access - we'll need a sandbox account for Redwood (temporary keys) and an empty VPC peering plan if doing private eval. also need whitelisting for our corp proxies.
15:34 Maya: we'll provision a trial Dedicated cluster and temporary API keys, and share instructions for VPC peering checklist.
15:40 Jordan: also note we'll run quantized model variants during bench to show CPU/GPU memory tradeoffs; quantization often reduces cost but may degrade quality slightly depending on model. we'll surface the delta.

17:10 Noah: any competitive concerns? we had a vendor who promised lower list prices but lacked the runtime tooling. we care about observability - token level cost breakdown, rollout control, and traceability.
17:22 Maya: Redwood console will provide per-route token cost breakdown, trace hooks and canary rollouts. we'll include screenshots in the follow-up deck.

19:05 Ravi: ok recap and next steps?
19:10 Maya: recap - artifacts to share: pricing scenarios (Maya), benchmark plan + prompts (Jordan), security pack (Maya), sample prompt set & prod traces (BluePeak - Emily). POC timeline week-by-week and owners as listed.
19:25 Ravi: agreed. we'll aim for the 72h benchmark in week 2 and decision end of week 3.
19:32 Maya: i'll follow up with the calendar invites and confirm bench start dates.
19:36 Jordan: i'll send the benchmark runbook and perf scripts.
19:40 Emily: i'll deliver the anonymized traces by Tuesday.

20:00 End of call.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: pricing-sheet.xlsx (sent after call), redwood-bench-runbook.md (Jordan), bluepeak-prod-trace-sample.csv (customer), redwood-security-pack.pdf

Action items (textual): Maya to send pricing scenarios, Jordan to send bench plan, Emily to provide traces, Ravi to confirm success criteria & budget threshold.

Transcription notes: some speaker labels merged, occasional word swap (K V cache sometimes transcribed as K V cash), numbers double-checked in follow-up materials.
